nodes.label: Lead Management & Automations implementation specification (unimplemented, dated 2026-05-22)
Positioning: Drive247 is a rental operating system with a CRM built in (vs Rental Pal Pro's GoHighLevel CRM)
Locked decisions: new leads table, V1 scope, fixed apply schema, opt-in tenant modules
Lead Management module — first-class lead-to-rental pipeline
Automations module — independent trigger + ordered-step workflow engine
Lead stage state machine — 17 stages with an explicit allowed-transition table
System-driven stage auto-transitions (verification, offer, BoldSign, Stripe, cron staleness)
Stage validation is split: DB trigger only stamps stage_updated_at, the TS lib enforces legality
Customer Apply flow — 7-step public application wizard on the booking site
Apply form Zod schema — one master schema shared by client steps and server validation
lead-documents storage bucket + presigned client-side upload before submission
Honeypot field + 5-per-IP-per-hour rate limit on public application submission
Portal lead Kanban board with drag-drop stage moves and realtime card movement
Rationale: 17 stages collapse into 8 visible columns + tabs — MUST NOT display 16 columns
3-column lead workspace — full page (MUST NOT be a drawer), collapses to tabs under 1400px
Left column — application summary, documents, tags, internal notes, activity timeline
Middle column — unified multi-channel inbox (SMS / email / WhatsApp / notes / system events)
Composer with channel toggle, template picker, {{variable}} autocomplete and action-link attachments
Inbound message routing — resolve lead by normalised phone/email, else create an inbound_* lead
Right column — AI next action, matching engine, running automations and quick actions
Quick actions wiring the lead workspace into existing Veriff / Bonzah / BoldSign / Stripe rails
Vehicle matching engine — deterministic ranked options from availability, price and closeness
Stitched (2-vehicle) and conditional (date-shift / higher-deposit) match options
AI rerank layer over matches — 60% deterministic / 40% aiScore, deterministic fallback on failure
Customisable offer link — curated vehicles + flexible dates behind an 8-char short code
Rationale: offers MUST NOT lock vehicles (would block other operators) — re-check availability only at acceptance
Blacklist engine — hard/soft matching on normalised phone, email, licence and fuzzy name
Dedup & merge — repeat submissions append to the existing lead instead of creating a new one
Lead → customer → rental conversion in a single transaction
One conversation row survives conversion — lead_id and customer_id both set, never a second thread
Lead scoring — lead_score 0-100 plus hot/warm/cold/risk band with score_reason
Trigger registry — code-defined lead.* event catalogue with payload variables and JSONB filters
Rationale: the portal TS registry and the Deno _shared registry MUST be kept in sync (JSON-as-truth if needed)
Automation step types — sms, email, wait, condition (safe whitelisted evaluator), stop
React Flow drag-drop automation builder with 500ms debounced auto-save drafts (no Save button)
Automation test mode — dry-run against a real lead, previews sends and simulates waits
Draft / published / archived lifecycle with versioned published_snapshot
Rationale: the engine reads the frozen published_snapshot, not live steps, so editing never breaks an in-flight run
Automation execution engine — event queue to runs to steps
emitEvent shared helper — the single sanctioned way app code queues an automation event
Minute-cadence event processor — matches published automations to queued events and starts runs
Wait-step resumption — same cron scans waiting runs with resume_at <= NOW()
Run cancellation — conversion stops running automations, deletion cascades app-level, pause is honoured by cron
Manual attach — operator force-starts an automation on a specific lead from the right column
leads table — the pre-rental opportunity record replacing enquiries
lead_documents table — uploaded lead files with verification_status lifecycle
lead_notes table — staff-only pinned/threaded notes never sent to the lead
lead_activity table — append-only actor-tagged audit feed behind the timeline
conversations table — one thread keyed by lead_id and/or customer_id
conversation_messages table — channel-agnostic message log with provider ids and delivery status
lead_offers table — short-code offer with curated vehicles JSONB, flex window, view and acceptance tracking
blacklist_entries table — tenant-scoped denylist keyed on any one of phone/email/licence
automations table — trigger definition plus frozen published_snapshot and version
automation_steps table — self-referencing draft step tree with true/false branches
automation_runs table — one execution against a generic entity, with status and resume_at
automation_run_logs table — per-step executed/skipped/failed record with output
automation_event_queue table — durable inbox decoupling event emission from automation matching
lead_message_templates table — per-tenant SMS/email/WhatsApp templates by category
phone_normalised / email_lower written by DB trigger — the join key for dedup, blacklist and inbound routing
Postgres triggers emitting lead.created / lead.stage_changed / terminal events into the queue
supabase_realtime publication additions — leads, conversations, conversation_messages, lead_offers, automation_runs
RLS strategy — reuse get_user_tenant_id()/is_super_admin(), INSERT only via service_role, nested tables inherit by subquery
Legacy enquiries copied into leads as source='legacy_enquiry'; table kept but marked DEPRECATED
Rationale: MUST NOT run a pipeline parallel to enquiries — refactor its writes into leads and map 'resolved' to 'lost'
submit-application edge function — public entry point that validates, dedups, blacklists, scores and creates the lead
submit-quick-enquiry edge function — replaces submit-enquiry, writes leads with source='quick_enquiry'
check-blacklist-match edge function — normalise then hard/soft match identifiers
compute-lead-score edge function — derives lead_score and score_band from application_data and history
run-matching-engine edge function — deliberately recomputes on demand (no cache column in V1)
create-offer-link edge function — inserts the offer, advances the stage, dispatches and emits
view-offer edge function — public resolve by short_code with view-count tracking
accept-offer edge function — validates flex window, re-checks availability, 409s on vehicle_just_taken
convert-lead-to-rental edge function — creates customer + rental and relinks the conversation
send-lead-message edge function — one multi-channel outbound path (SMS/email/WhatsApp) into a conversation
inbound-sms-webhook edge function — Twilio SMS and WhatsApp share one handler with a channel branch
inbound-email-webhook edge function — resolves by email or In-Reply-To conversation id
automation-trigger-event edge function — queues an event from app code or as a DB-trigger fallback
automation-execute-step edge function — service_role-only single step executor
automation-poll-pending cron function — 100 events + 100 resumable runs per 60s pass, guarded by X-Cron-Secret
automation-publish edge function — validates the graph (no orphans, no cycles, both branches) then snapshots
ai-suggest-next-action edge function — stage-specific playbook, returns do_nothing below 0.6 confidence
ai-rank-matches edge function — scores match options, cache key leadId + hash(options)
ai-draft-message edge function — drafts in the tenant's communication_tone
ai-extract-from-conversation edge function — mines the thread for application_data fields above 0.7 confidence
AI layer principles — structured output only, never a chatbot, deterministic fallback, 5-minute cache, logged calls
Per-tenant AI monthly quota with hard stop; AI usage billing deferred to a separate project
Reuse map — the source of truth listing existing Drive247 surfaces that MUST NOT be re-implemented
New manager tab keys leads/automations; publishing restricted to admin/head_admin inside the edge function
Tenant flags — lead_management_enabled, automations_enabled, stale/auto-lost thresholds, communication_tone
seed_default_lead_templates(tenant_id) — default templates seeded when a tenant enables the module
{{variable}} catalog for lead templates, rendered server-side by the same engine as lockbox templates
Outbound routing — queue the message row first, dispatch per channel, let the provider webhook settle status
Realtime subscription map + useRealtimeInvalidate query-invalidation pattern
Per-lead presence channel so staff see teammates viewing the same lead
Phasing — Phase 1 Lead Hub MVP, Phase 2 Automations module, Phase 3 AI rerank/extraction, Phase 4 form builder
V1 hardcoded automations (welcome SMS, stale reminders, auto-lost at 7d, offer expiry) later migrated into the builder
GIVEN/WHEN/THEN acceptance criteria used as the QA contract
Anti-patterns — 17 explicit prohibitions binding the implementation
Rationale: never copy the competitor's insurance-PDF editing workflow — a legal landmine; store official documents only
Linear 11-stage implementation checklist for the building agent
Reuse of the lockbox_templates {{variable}} rendering + template-editor pattern
Reuse of the portal RealtimeChatContext channel/presence pattern
Reuse of the cmd-poll-pending cron-polling pattern
Reuse of the gig-driver-images storage bucket + policy pattern
Reuse of existing verification and payment rails (Veriff/AI-OCR/face-match/CMD, Bonzah, BoldSign, Stripe preauth/checkout)
Portal manager-permission tab-key registry (TAB_KEYS / TAB_GROUPS / ROUTE_TAB_MAP)

Event emission → durable queue → cron matcher → run → snapshot step execution → logs
